Answer: B
Reason: The chest radiograph shows diffuse, bilateral micronodular opacities creating a "sandstorm" appearance with prominent calcification along the pleural surfaces (indicated by arrows), which is pathognomonic for pulmonary alveolar microlithiasis; this condition is also characteristically associated with a clinical-radiological dissociation where patients remain asymptomatic despite extensive radiographic findings.
